evidence.upstream_commit: 9122c5235ec8 [RISCV] Enable bidirectional scheduling and tracking register pressure (#115445): ancestor of llvmorg-20.1.8, not of llvmorg-19.1.7 (in range). --stat confirms it adds RISCVSubtarget::overrideSchedPolicy (RISCVSubtarget.cpp/.h), which matches the note's claim.
evidence.root_cause_confirmed: FREP_O/FREP_I (RISCVInstrInfoXfrep.td:35-44) are hasSideEffects=0, mayLoad=0, mayStore=0, Sched<[]>, and SNITCHFrepLoops.cpp:510/526 inserts them pre-RA (pass runs at RISCVTargetMachine.cpp:623, before machine-scheduler). Nothing tied the body's position to the frep. The only reason 19 was correct is that the pre-RA scheduler ran bottom-up only. Reproduced with build/int-20/bin/llc: at all four opt levels, fmul.d is hoisted above li/frep.o in main and main1 (both frep loops), so frep.o repeats the wrong 2 instructions. This is a real miscompile.
evidence.fix_matches_fork_precedent: The fix is two case labels in the fork's own RISCVInstrInfo::isSchedulingBoundary switch (RISCVInstrInfo.cpp:3252-3261), next to LOOP0setup/LOOP1setup/LOOP0setupi/LOOP1setupi, which the fork already marks as boundaries for the same reason (the PULP hardware-loop setup fixes the loop body's position). The hook is standard: upstream targets use TargetInstrInfo::isSchedulingBoundary for instructions that code must not move across. The upstream scheduling policy is left alone, which is the right call; overriding overrideSchedPolicy for Snitch would revert upstream's decision for a whole CPU. Upstream RISC-V/CORE-V has no repeat-next-N instruction, so the XCV rule-12 reference does not apply, and the note says so.

evidence.gap_after_frep: Not covered, and it is a separate issue. A boundary only cuts the block at the frep. Everything after it, the N body instructions and any later non-body instructions in the same block, is still one scheduling region. So an independent instruction could in principle be interleaved into the repeated body. This gap already existed at LLVM 19 (the bottom-up scheduler had no constraint either), and 9122c5235ec8 did not introduce it. I probed it with a variant of @main that adds independent integer and FP work (mul/xor/store volatile, fmul/fsd) to the same block after the frep body: at -O2 the body (fmul.d, fadd.d) stays immediately after frep.o, and bidirectional scheduling only reorders the non-body instructions among themselves. In practice the body is protected by its own data dependences, not by any structural guarantee. A robust fix (bundling the frep and its N body instructions, or ending the region after the Nth instruction) belongs in a separate task, together with a fork test whose body contains independent instructions. It should not block this commit.
